dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt system (JMA standard receipt software), compiled with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL on Linux. Uses COPY with .INC copybooks, ASSIGN to symbolic names, INDEXED files with FILE STATUS — typical ORCA/NACL coding style.
evidence: no EXEC CICS / no EXEC SQL
fixed-format source with Japanese EUC comments

purpose.domain_detail: Japanese medical insurance receipt (レセプト) processing system — inpatient (入院) receipt print file creation, part of the JMA ORCA open-source medical billing system
purpose.summary: ORCR0730 creates print files for inpatient medical insurance receipts (入院レセプト印刷用ファイル作成). It reads multiple indexed RECE6x files, processes insurance history, co-payment amounts, special notes, and regional public-expense data, then writes formatted output for receipt printing. The program has an extensive revision history spanning 2008–2014 covering numerous Japanese regional insurance rule changes.

notable_features: Multiple INDEXED files with SEQUENTIAL and DYNAMIC access
Extensive revision history with named developers (NACL-Fujiwara, NACL-Kadowaki)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS — pure file-based batch
No COMP-3 usage despite financial calculations
verdict.notes: Source is encoded in EUC-JP (Japanese) but decoded as latin-1, causing mojibake in comments. The program is clearly part of the well-known JMA ORCA open-source medical receipt system used widely in Japanese clinics. File name ORCR0730.CBL and program-id ORCR0730 are consistent with ORCA naming conventions. The absence of COMP-3 is unusual for financial data but consistent with ORCA's GnuCOBOL usage patterns.
